label: KV — Preflight Pictorial Visual Inspection

slides.n:
DO:
Time: 2:00 total (KV 0:50, Briefing 1:10; AQPM Table 5.1.3).
Start in the CQMT2.1 Briefing/Debriefing deck with the intro slides: About Today (including document verification, FOM 3.1) and Flow of the Day.
At the deck's KV slide, open this file and one Airplane Systems and Limitations set (1 to 5), and complete them in either order (KV 0:50 for both parts).
Give this part to one pilot at a time. AQPM QS 12.8.1 (p.4.5.171): "The pilot will individually demonstrate the ability to conduct the pictorial visual inspection." 8900.1 Vol 3, Ch 19, Sec 7, para 3-1280C2 (CHG 940): "The visual inspection must be completed individually by each pilot. Pilots may not complete the visual inspection in a group environment."
For each item, the pilot describes what indications they are looking for to determine if the item is acceptable or not (8900.1 Vol 3, Ch 19, Sec 7, para 3-1280C5).
When both parts are complete, return to the CQMT2.1 deck and complete the briefing (Briefing 1:10).

NOTE: If one crewmember is unsatisfactory, the remaining crewmember completes training per the crew pairing procedures found in AQPM chapter 1, Crew Scheduling and Pairing Policy (AQPM 4.3).

Time to Work Through This PPT Deck: shared with the Airplane Systems and Limitations KV (KV 0:50 for both parts, AQPM Table 5.1.3).
Sequence: CQMT2.1 deck intro slides first (About Today, Flow of the Day); then this file and one Airplane Systems and Limitations set, in either order; then return to the CQMT2.1 deck and complete the briefing (Briefing 1:10).

slides.t: Main gear doors open with the door release handle in the doors closed position
slides.n:
DO: Ask the question below. When the pilot has answered, click once to show the abnormal condition.

ASK:
What do you check on the landing gear doors, and where must the door release handle be when a gear door is open? FCOM Vol 1 NP
ANSWER:
Landing gear door position (FCOM Vol 1 NP)
When any gear door is open, the respective door handle release must be in the "doors open" position (WARNING, FCOM Vol 1 NP)
If the handle is in the "doors closed" position and the doors are open, pressurizing hydraulic system 1 or 4 will close the doors and can result in personal injury (WARNING, FCOM Vol 1 NP)
ABNORMAL (shown on click):
Main gear doors open with the door release handle in the "doors closed" position (unsafe). FCOM standard: with a gear door open, the door handle release is in the "doors open" position (WARNING, FCOM Vol 1 NP).

DO: Use the inspection route at right; the slides that follow are in route order. No click on this slide.

ASK:
Who may accomplish the exterior inspection, and what conditions do you look for at every location? FCOM Vol 1 NP
ANSWER:
Either crewmember may accomplish the exterior inspection; relief pilots may be assigned the exterior preflight (FCOM Vol 1 NP)
Before each flight the captain, first officer, or maintenance crew must verify the airplane is satisfactory for flight; items at each location may be checked in any sequence (FCOM Vol 1 NP)
Surfaces and structures clear, not damaged, not missing parts, and no fluid leaks
Tires not too worn, not damaged, and no tread separation
Gear struts not fully compressed
Engine inlets and tailpipes clear, access panels secured, exterior not damaged, and reversers stowed
Doors and access panels not in use latched
Probes, vents, and static ports clear and not damaged; skin adjacent to the pitot probes and static ports not wrinkled
Antennas not damaged; light lenses clean and not damaged (FCOM Vol 1 NP)

slides.t: Security Inspection and Emergency and Safety Equipment
The Security Inspection is required prior to each departure. The Emergency and Safety Equi
slides.n:
DO: Read the slide with the pilot. No click on this slide.

ASK:
When is the security inspection required, what does it consist of, and when is the emergency equipment preflight done? FCOM Vol 1 NP
ANSWER:
A security inspection is required prior to each departure; it is a physical search of areas for any suspicious items or personnel (FCOM Vol 1 NP)
The Emergency and Safety Equipment Preflight Procedures are normally accomplished in conjunction with the Security Inspection (FCOM Vol 1 NP)
The flight deck emergency systems and equipment are inspected by the flight crew prior to the first flight of the flight crew on an aircraft during a duty period, or if the aircraft has been left unattended by a flight crew for any period of time (FCOM Vol 1 NP)
Upper deck items apply to freighters, and to passenger airplanes without cabin crew (FCOM Vol 1 NP); on passenger airplanes, the cabin emergency equipment preflight may be delegated to the cabin crew (FCOM Vol 1 NP)

ANSWER:
Supernumerary/Jumpseat briefing (n/a to Company 747 flight crew): complete; provide the briefing cards and the pictorial safety card, show the Life Vest Video, and ensure each flight deck occupant understands the oxygen and interphone systems and the Sterile Flight Deck procedure
Supernumerary area: secured; secure equipment and any loose items
Galley(s): secured; secure galley equipment and any loose items; verify catering is on board
Smoke barrier door: closed and locked; lock all three security locks (if installed) by moving the latches to the locked position
The door should be locked prior to engine start and not opened until engine shutdown unless cargo handlers require access to the main deck for livestock needs, or an emergency situation and/or evacuation is necessary; all non-crewmembers must be briefed on flight deck security access, and if the main deck is accessed in flight the security locks are returned to the locked position
400C, PAX (without cabin crew): upper deck emergency door(s): select
LCF: L1 door mode selector: select ARM / AUTOMATIC

NOTE: Only the visual items of the Final Flight Deck Preparation are covered in this KV; the RVSM check, ATC clearance, fuel, and flight documentation (FCOM Vol 1 NP) are not pictorial items.
